Render error when combining multiple input parameters in docstring **Describe the bug & Reproduce** My team is writing a function in Python, which contains 3 inputs that are similar, so we want to put them in the same line in the docstring. As described in 4. Parameters in [numpydoc docstring guide](https://numpydoc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/format.html#sections), this is possible if you write something like this: ``` x1, x2 : array_like Input arrays, description of `x1`, `x2`. ``` However, this produces: Even worse, when added "optional", the rendered HTML stays the same as the screenshot above, so there is no way to tell whether it is optional: ``` x1, x2 : array_like, optional Input arrays, description of `x1`, `x2`. ``` **Expected behavior** Something like - x1, x2 (_array_like, optional_) - Input arrays, description of x1, x2. **Environment info** - OS: macOS 10.15.5 (19F101) - Python version: 3.7.7 - Sphinx version: 3.0.3. - Extra tools: browser: Firefox 79.0a1 or Safari 13.1.1 - Sphinx extensions: ``` extensions = [ "sphinx.ext.autodoc", "sphinx.ext.todo", "sphinx.ext.coverage", "sphinx.ext.extlinks", "sphinx.ext.intersphinx", "sphinx.ext.mathjax", "sphinx.ext.viewcode", "sphinx.ext.napoleon", "nbsphinx", "sphinx.ext.mathjax", "sphinxcontrib.bibtex", "sphinx.ext.doctest", ] ``` # Plan ## Problem The bug is in the napoleon extension: `sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py`. A numpydoc parameter line such as: ``` x1, x2 : array_like, optional Input arrays, description of `x1`, `x2`. ``` is parsed with the whole comma-joined string `x1, x2` as the parameter name. With napoleon's default configuration the field formatter emits invalid RST field directives: ``` :param x1, x2: Input arrays, description of x1, x2. :type x1, x2: :class:`array_like`, *optional* ``` Field names cannot contain a comma, so docutils does not interpret these as `param`/`type` fields for `x1` or `x2`. The rendered output shows the raw text and loses the `optional` qualifier — exactly the screenshot in the report. ## Why the previous fix did not cover this Commit `849d3c18a`/`64a26ff4d` (PR #7799, "parameters are not escaped for combined params in numpydoc") added comma-splitting in `NumpyDocstring._escape_args_and_kwargs` (`docstring.py:1082-1087`). That helper escapes each comma-separated name individually. It fixes the `napoleon_use_param=False` code path, which goes through `_format_field` and produces `**x1, x2** (*array_like*) -- ...` (that renders acceptably). The default path is `napoleon_use_param=True` (`napoleon/__init__.py:268`). It goes through `_format_docutils_params` (`docstring.py:389`), which was never updated to split multi-name parameters. It builds one `:param :` per field using the still-comma-joined `_name`. That is the broken output in the report. ## Proposed change Split comma-separated parameter names into separate RST fields in `_format_docutils_params` (`docstring.py:389-405`). For each consumed field whose name contains `", "`: - Emit a `:param :` (and its description block) for each name. - Emit a `:type : ` for each name, reusing the same `_type` string. Concretely, replace the single-`_name` body with a loop over `_name.split(", ")`. The existing block-formatting helpers (`_format_block`, `_fix_field_desc`, `_strip_empty`) stay as they are; only the name is split. For the reported example with `napoleon_use_param=True` this yields: ``` :param x1: Input arrays, description of x1, x2. :type x1: :class:`array_like`, *optional* :param x2: Input arrays, description of x1, x2. :type x2: :class:`array_like`, *optional* ``` This is the standard way to document several names that share a type and description; it renders as two separate parameter entries, each with the type and the `optional` marker. The `napoleon_use_param=False` display path needs no change: `_format_field` already emits `**x1, x2** (*array_like, optional*) -- ...`, which renders correctly (verified by parsing that line with docutils). ## Scope and evidence - `_format_docutils_params` (`docstring.py:389`) is the only formatter that builds `:param:`/`:type:` directives, so the fix is localized there. It is used for parameters, attributes, and other-parameters sections, so multi-name splitting will apply consistently to those sections. - `_consume_field` already stores `_name` unmodified (only `_escape_args_and_kwargs` mangles `*`/`**` prefixes), so splitting on `", "` at format time is safe and preserves escaping. - Existing tests live in `tests/test_ext_napoleon_docstring.py`; related ones are `test_parameters_without_class_reference` (line 1343) and `test_parameters_with_class_reference` (line 1320), which exercise both `napoleon_use_param` settings. The multiline-description case in the report should be added as a new test covering both `napoleon_use_param=False` and `True`. ## Steps 1. Update `_format_docutils_params` in `sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py` to iterate over `_name.split(", ")` when building the `:param:` and `:type:` lines, keeping shared `_type` and description for each split name. 2. Add a test in `tests/test_ext_napoleon_docstring.py` using the numpydoc multi-name line (e.g. `x1, x2 : array_like, optional`) and assert the expected field output for both settings of `napoleon_use_param`. 3. Add a `CHANGES` entry under the current release's napoleon fixes. ## Open items to confirm during implementation - Whether the field order should be `:param x1:`/`:type x1:`/`:param x2:`/`:type x2:` (per-name pairs) or grouped `:param x1:`/`:param x2:`/`:type x1:`/`:type x2:`. The per-name pairing above matches how each entry renders as one parameter and keeps the type adjacent to its name; if the existing single-parameter ordering convention suggests otherwise, keep the emit order consistent with the current code (each name's `param` then its `type`). - Verify the `napoleon_use_param=False` path already renders `optional` after a separate docutils/Sphinx build; if a separate display defect exists there it is not caused by `_format_docutils_params` and should be tracked separately rather than folded into this change.
